claim: Collective cell migration plays an essential role in vertebrate development.
source: Collective cell migration plays an essential role in vertebrate development, yet the extent to which dynamically changing microenvironments influence this phenomenon remains unclear.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that draws from established scientific consensus about the importance of collective cell migration in development.

claim: FN protein expression within the mesoderm is unorganized and punctate prior to cranial NCC emigration.
source: FN protein expression within the mesoderm is unorganized and punctate prior to cranial NCC emigration, but filamentous after it has been traversed by leader cells
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations described in the Results section and shown in Figure 1.

claim: FN becomes filamentous after leader NCCs invade.
source: FN protein expression within the mesoderm is unorganized and punctate prior to cranial NCC emigration, but filamentous after it has been traversed by leader cells
evidence: This is directly stated in the Results section heading and supported by microscopy data in Figure 1.

claim: Punctate FN is found both distal to the invasive NCC migratory front and adjacent to the leader NCC subpopulation.
source: Punctate FN, not yet fibrils, are found both distal to the invasive NCC migratory front and adjacent to the leader NCC subpopulation (Figure 1C).
evidence: This observation is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 1C showing the punctate FN distribution.

claim: Elongated FN fibrils are located behind the leading edge of invasive NCC streams.
source: By contrast, elongated FN fibrils are located behind the leading edge of invasive NCC streams (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by microscopy images in Figure 1D.

claim: FN fibrils proximal to the invasive NCC migratory front did not reveal a preferred directional orientation.
source: FN fibrils proximal to the invasive NCC migratory front did not reveal a preferred directional orientation.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data described in the Results section.

claim: Similar punctate FN was visible in regions outside the NCC migratory pathway, subjacent to the surface ectoderm.
source: Similar punctate FN was also visible in regions outside the NCC migratory pathway, subjacent to the surface ectoderm (Figure 1C).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1C.

claim: Knockdown of FN expression introduced into premigratory NCCs within the neural tube led to a significant reduction (nearly 30%) in the total distance migrated by NCCs enroute to BA2.
source: Knockdown of FN expression introduced into premigratory NCCs within the neural tube led to a significant reduction (nearly 30%) in the total distance migrated by NCCs enroute to BA2 (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is a direct experimental result from loss-of-function experiments shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Microinjection of soluble FN into the cranial NCC migratory domain led to a dramatic reduction (by 70%) in NCC migration as indicated by a decrease in the area typically covered by the invading NCCs.
source: Microinjection of soluble FN into the cranial NCC migratory domain, for example, into the paraxial mesoderm adjacent to rhombomere 4 (r4) prior to NCC delamination, also led to a dramatic reduction (by 70%) in NCC migration as indicated by a decrease in the area typically covered by the invading NCCs (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is a direct experimental result from gain-of-function experiments shown in Figure 1F.

claim: A balance of FN within the migratory microenvironment is required to promote proper migration.
source: We conclude that a balance of FN within the migratory microenvironment is required to promote proper migration.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the experimental results showing that both decreasing and increasing FN levels impair migration.

claim: The agent-based model can generate a single anisotropically migrating stream over a simulated time of 12 hr.
source: Individual snapshots (A) of an example ABM realization reveals that the model can generate a single anisotropically migrating stream over a simulated time of 12 hr.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the simulation results shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Different realizations of the ABM using the same parameter values but different random seeds may produce streams that exhibit the formation of multiple branches.
source: Different realizations generated using the same parameter values but different random seeds (B), however, may produce streams that exhibit the formation of multiple branches and demonstrate the range of possible model behaviors.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2B and demonstrates the stochastic nature of the model.

claim: ECM remodeling, haptotaxis, contact guidance, and cell-cell repulsion are sufficient for cells to establish streams in silico.
source: ECM remodeling, haptotaxis, contact guidance, and cell-cell repulsion are sufficient for cells to establish streams in silico, however, additional mechanisms, such as chemotaxis, are required to consistently guide cells along the correct target corridor.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the computational modeling results described in the abstract and Results section.

claim: Additional mechanisms, such as chemotaxis, are required to consistently guide cells along the correct target corridor.
source: ECM remodeling, haptotaxis, contact guidance, and cell-cell repulsion are sufficient for cells to establish streams in silico, however, additional mechanisms, such as chemotaxis, are required to consistently guide cells along the correct target corridor.
evidence: This is inferred from model simulations showing that streams branch without additional guidance mechanisms.

claim: Contact guidance and differential cell-cell repulsion between leader and follower cells are key contributors to robust collective cell migration by preventing stream breakage.
source: Further model investigations imply that contact guidance and differential cell-cell repulsion between leader and follower cells are key contributors to robust collective cell migration by preventing stream breakage.
evidence: This is concluded from simulated rescue experiments described in the Results section and shown in Figure 5.

claim: Long-distance migration without jamming is most likely to occur when leading cells specialize in creating ECM fibers, and trailing cells specialize in responding to environmental cues by upregulating mechanisms such as contact guidance.
source: Global sensitivity analysis and simulated gain- and loss-of-function experiments suggest that long-distance migration without jamming is most likely to occur when leading cells specialize in creating ECM fibers, and trailing cells specialize in responding to environmental cues by upregulating mechanisms such as contact guidance.
evidence: This is concluded from the computational experiments shown in Figures 3 and 5.

claim: Vertebrate neural crest cells (NCCs) are an important model for collective cell migration.
source: Vertebrate neural crest cells (NCCs) are an important model for collective cell migration.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: Discrete streams of migratory NCCs distribute throughout the embryo to contribute to nearly every organ.
source: Discrete streams of migratory NCCs distribute throughout the embryo to contribute to nearly every organ (Le Douarin and Kalcheim, 1999; Tang and Bronner, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Mistakes in NCC migration may result in severe birth defects, termed neurocristopathies.
source: Consequently, mistakes in NCC migration may result in severe birth defects, termed neurocristopathies (Vega-Lopez et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Several invasive mesenchymal cancers resemble collective NCC migration, with cells moving away from the tumor mass in chain-like arrays or narrow strands.
source: Moreover, several invasive mesenchymal cancers resemble collective NCC migration, with cells moving away from the tumor mass in chain-like arrays or narrow strands (Friedl et al., 2004; Friedl and Alexander, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Leader NCCs in discrete migratory streams in the head, gut, and trunk are highly exploratory.
source: Time-lapse analyses of NCC migratory behaviors in several embryo model organisms have revealed that leader NCCs in discrete migratory streams in the head (Teddy and Kulesa, 2004; Genuth et al., 2018), gut (Druckenbrod and Epstein, 2007; Young et al., 2014), and trunk (Kasemeier-Kulesa et al., 2005; Li et al., 2019) are highly exploratory.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous experimental studies.

claim: Leading NCCs extend thin filopodial protrusions in many directions, interact with the ECM and other cell types, then select a preferred direction for invasion.
source: Leading NCCs extend thin filopodial protrusions in many directions, interact with the ECM and other cell types, then select a preferred direction for invasion.
evidence: This is based on time-lapse analyses cited in the previous sentence.

claim: Trailing cells extend protrusions to contact leaders and other cells to maintain cell neighbor relationships and move collectively.
source: Trailing cells extend protrusions to contact leaders and other cells to maintain cell neighbor relationships and move collectively (Kulesa et al., 2008; Ridenour et al., 2014; Richardson et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous experimental studies.

claim: A leader-follower model for NCC migration suggests that NCCs at the front of migrating collectives read out guidance signals and communicate over long distances with trailing cells.
source: These observations suggest a leader-follower model for NCC migration (McLennan et al., 2012) in which NCCs at the front of migrating collectives read out guidance signals and communicate over long distances with trailing cells.
evidence: This is a model proposed in previous work and cited here.

claim: Chick leader cranial NCCs show enhanced expression of secreted factors, such as angiopoietin-2 (Ang-2) and fibronectin (FN).
source: In support of this, chick leader cranial NCCs show enhanced expression of secreted factors, such as angiopoietin-2 (Ang-2) (McLennan et al., 2015a) and fibronectin (FN) (Morrison et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous experimental studies.

claim: Knockdown of Ang-2 reduces the chemokinetic behavior of follower chick NCCs, resulting in disrupted collective cell migration.
source: Knockdown of Ang-2 reduces the chemokinetic behavior of follower chick NCCs, resulting in disrupted collective cell migration (McKinney et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous experimental study.

claim: NCCs cultured in FN-rich ECM move with thin, anchored filopodia through a field that is punctate immediately distal to the migrating front.
source: NCCs cultured in FN-rich ECM move with thin, anchored filopodia through a field that is punctate immediately distal to the migrating front, while 'pioneer' NCCs within the front appear to form radially oriented bundles of FN-containing filaments (Rovasio et al., 1983).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous in vitro study.

claim: Pioneer NCCs within the front appear to form radially oriented bundles of FN-containing filaments.
source: NCCs cultured in FN-rich ECM move with thin, anchored filopodia through a field that is punctate immediately distal to the migrating front, while 'pioneer' NCCs within the front appear to form radially oriented bundles of FN-containing filaments (Rovasio et al., 1983).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous in vitro study.

claim: Inhibition of ECM-integrin receptors resulted in delamination of NCCs into the neural tube lumen.
source: Later work on the NCC epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition showed that inhibition of ECM-integrin receptors resulted in delamination of NCCs into the neural tube lumen (Kil et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous experimental study.

claim: FN is abundant in the mouse head and neck.
source: Moreover, FN is abundant in the mouse head and neck (Mittal et al., 2010), and there is a dramatic reduction in the number of migrating NCCs that reach the heart in FN null mice (Wang and Astrof, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: There is a dramatic reduction in the number of migrating NCCs that reach the heart in FN null mice.
source: Moreover, FN is abundant in the mouse head and neck (Mittal et al., 2010), and there is a dramatic reduction in the number of migrating NCCs that reach the heart in FN null mice (Wang and Astrof, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous experimental study.

claim: FN is critical for NCC to reach their targets.
source: Thus, FN is critical for NCC to reach their targets, although its precise role in collective cell migration remains unclear.
evidence: This is inferred from the cited experimental evidence showing reduced NCC migration in FN null mice.

claim: Previous models for NCC migration demonstrated that contact guidance can establish collective behavior and create single-file cell chains.
source: Previous models for NCC migration demonstrated that contact guidance, a mechanism by which cells align themselves along ECM fibers, can establish collective behavior and create single-file cell chains (Painter, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous modeling study.

claim: Later models incorporating ECM degradation and haptotaxis demonstrated how matrix heterogeneity and cell-cell interactions could determine cell migratory patterns.
source: Later models incorporating ECM degradation and haptotaxis, a process by which cells migrate up adhesive ECM gradients, demonstrated how matrix heterogeneity and cell-cell interactions could determine cell migratory patterns (Painter et al., 2010; Wynn et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous modeling studies.

claim: Models for other collectively migrating cells suggest that ECM remodeling by motile cells can enable anisotropic collective movement, with migratory directions dictated by fiber orientation.
source: Models for other collectively migrating cells, such as fibroblasts, suggest that ECM remodeling by motile cells can enable anisotropic collective movement, with migratory directions dictated by fiber orientation (Dallon et al., 1999; Groh and Louis, 2010; Chauviere et al., 2010; Azimzade et al., 2019; Wershof et al., 2019; Pramanik et al., 2021; Suveges et al., 2021; Metzcar et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple previous modeling studies.

claim: No models have yet addressed how collective migration arises from cell remodeling of an initially isotropic, immature ECM.
source: No models have yet addressed how collective migration arises from cell remodeling of an initially isotropic, immature ECM.
evidence: This is a statement about the gap in the literature that this study addresses.

claim: Observations of the ABM indicate that ECM remodeling, haptotaxis, contact guidance, and cell-cell repulsion can generate stream-like patterns.
source: Observations of individual ABM simulations indicate that ECM remodeling, haptotaxis, contact guidance, and cell-cell repulsion can generate stream-like patterns, with secretory cells able to maintain their positions at the front of the stream (Figure 2A; Figure 2—video 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the simulation results shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Secretory cells are able to maintain their positions at the front of the stream in the ABM.
source: Observations of individual ABM simulations indicate that ECM remodeling, haptotaxis, contact guidance, and cell-cell repulsion can generate stream-like patterns, with secretory cells able to maintain their positions at the front of the stream (Figure 2A; Figure 2—video 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the simulation results shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Cells can migrate anisotropically in the ABM, even though the initial FN lattice is isotropic.
source: Cells can migrate anisotropically, even though the initial FN lattice is isotropic, and trailing cell velocities are oriented toward leader cells (for instance, the average angle that the follower cell velocity vector makes with the horizontal axis is 0.11 radians, or 6 degrees, for the simulation shown in Figure 2A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the simulation results and quantitative analysis.

claim: Trailing cell velocities are oriented toward leader cells in the ABM.
source: Cells can migrate anisotropically, even though the initial FN lattice is isotropic, and trailing cell velocities are oriented toward leader cells (for instance, the average angle that the follower cell velocity vector makes with the horizontal axis is 0.11 radians, or 6 degrees, for the simulation shown in Figure 2A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by quantitative analysis of the simulation results.

claim: Stream-like patterns in the ABM leave most ECM fibers aligned parallel to the horizontal axis.
source: Stream-like patterns leave most ECM fibers aligned parallel to the horizontal axis, that is, the direction of the target corridor (Figure 2—figure supplements 3–4; Figure 2—video 3).
evidence: This is demonstrated by analysis of fiber orientations in the simulations shown in Figure 2—figure supplements 3–4.

claim: In some cases, ABM streams split into two or more 'branches' that colonize regions along the vertical axis.
source: In some cases, ABM streams split into two or more 'branches' that colonize regions along the vertical axis (Figure 2B; Figure 2—videos 2 and 4).
evidence: This is demonstrated by simulation results shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Streams split in the ABM because there is no signal specifically guiding NCCs in a direction parallel to the horizontal axis.
source: Streams split because there is no signal specifically guiding NCCs in a direction parallel to the horizontal axis.
evidence: This is an inference from the model structure and simulation results.

claim: Additional signals are required to prevent NCC stream branching in the ABM.
source: We conclude that additional signals are required to prevent NCC stream branching.
evidence: This is concluded from the observation that streams branch in the absence of directional guidance.

claim: The distance NCCs travel in the horizontal direction is most sensitive to χ, the parameter determining the degree to which NCC directional migration in response to the FN matrix is dominated by haptotaxis or contact guidance.
source: The resulting Sobol indices indicate that the distance NCCs travel in the horizontal direction (i.e. along the target corridor) is most sensitive to χ, the parameter determining the degree to which NCC directional migration in response to the FN matrix is dominated by haptotaxis (χ=1), contact guidance (χ=0), or a linear combination of the two.
evidence: This is determined from the eFAST global sensitivity analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Increasing the value of χ decreases the distance cells travel in the ABM.
source: Increasing the value of this parameter decreases the distance cells travel (partial Spearman rank correlation coefficient, PRCC: –0.91, p<0.0001).
evidence: This is determined from correlation analysis of the simulation results.

claim: When contact guidance dominates the cell-ECM force (χ<0.5), increasing the cell-cell repulsion strength decreases the distance that the streams migrate.
source: Subsequent analysis of its scatter plot (Figure 2D) reveals that when contact guidance dominates the cell-ECM force (χ<0.5), increasing the cell-cell repulsion strength decreases the distance that the streams migrate (PRCC: –0.64, p<0.0001).
evidence: This is determined from analysis of scatter plots shown in Figure 2D.

claim: When haptotaxis dominates the direction of the force (χ>0.8), the relationship between cell-cell repulsion and distance traveled is weaker but remains monotonically decreasing.
source: When haptotaxis dominates the direction of the force (χ>0.8), this relationship is weaker but remains monotonically decreasing (PRCC: –0.59, p<0.0001).
evidence: This is determined from correlation analysis of the simulation results.

claim: The distance traveled by NCCs is most sensitive to the mechanism by which cells respond to the ECM, with contact guidance favoring longer streams.
source: Hence, the distance traveled by NCCs is most sensitive to the mechanism by which cells respond to the ECM, with contact guidance favoring longer streams, while haptotaxis and cell-cell repulsion are negatively correlated with the distance that NCCs travel.
evidence: This is concluded from the global sensitivity analysis results.

claim: Haptotaxis and cell-cell repulsion are negatively correlated with the distance that NCCs travel.
source: Hence, the distance traveled by NCCs is most sensitive to the mechanism by which cells respond to the ECM, with contact guidance favoring longer streams, while haptotaxis and cell-cell repulsion are negatively correlated with the distance that NCCs travel.
evidence: This is concluded from the global sensitivity analysis results.

claim: The cell-ECM weight, χ, generates the largest Sobol indices for the lateral spread statistic.
source: The cell-ECM weight, χ, again generates the largest Sobol indices for this statistic and exhibits a strong negative monotonic relationship (PRCC: –0.90, p<0.0001), indicating that lateral migration increases with upregulation of contact guidance.
evidence: This is determined from the eFAST global sensitivity analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 6.

claim: Lateral migration increases with upregulation of contact guidance.
source: The cell-ECM weight, χ, again generates the largest Sobol indices for this statistic and exhibits a strong negative monotonic relationship (PRCC: –0.90, p<0.0001), indicating that lateral migration increases with upregulation of contact guidance.
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation analysis of the simulation results.

claim: The lateral spread statistic is weakly correlated with the filopodial radius.
source: By contrast, scatter plots suggest this statistic is weakly correlated with the filopodial radius (PRCC: 0.12) and cell-cell repulsion strength (PRCC: –0.08).
evidence: This is determined from correlation analysis of the simulation results.

claim: The lateral spread statistic is weakly correlated with cell-cell repulsion strength.
source: By contrast, scatter plots suggest this statistic is weakly correlated with the filopodial radius (PRCC: 0.12) and cell-cell repulsion strength (PRCC: –0.08).
evidence: This is determined from correlation analysis of the simulation results.

claim: The cell-ECM weight and the cell-cell repulsion strength parameter both yield significant first-order Sobol indices for the average distance between neighboring cells.
source: The cell-ECM weight and the cell-cell repulsion strength parameter both yield significant first-order Sobol indices (Figure 2—figure supplement 5), with the latter parameter generating larger values.
evidence: This is determined from the eFAST global sensitivity analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5.

claim: Only the total-order Sobol index is significant for the filopodial radius for the nearest neighbor distance statistic.
source: Only the total-order Sobol index is significant for the filopodial radius, which implies that this parameter affects cell-cell separation largely via its higher-order interactions with the other two parameters.
evidence: This is determined from the eFAST global sensitivity analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5.

claim: The filopodial radius affects cell-cell separation largely via its higher-order interactions with other parameters.
source: Only the total-order Sobol index is significant for the filopodial radius, which implies that this parameter affects cell-cell separation largely via its higher-order interactions with the other two parameters.
evidence: This is inferred from the pattern of Sobol indices.

claim: There is a monotonically decreasing relationship between the nearest neighbor distance and the cell-ECM weight, χ.
source: Scatter plots (Figure 2—figure supplement 5) suggest a monotonically decreasing relationship between the nearest neighbor distance and the cell-ECM weight, χ (PRCC: –0.74, p<0.0001), a monotonically increasing relationship with the cell-cell repulsion parameter, ci (PRCC: 0.78, p<0.0001) and almost no correlation for the filopodial radius (PRCC: 0.05, p=0.07).
evidence: This is determined from correlation analysis of the simulation results shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5.

claim: There is a monotonically increasing relationship between the nearest neighbor distance and the cell-cell repulsion parameter, ci.
source: Scatter plots (Figure 2—figure supplement 5) suggest a monotonically decreasing relationship between the nearest neighbor distance and the cell-ECM weight, χ (PRCC: –0.74, p<0.0001), a monotonically increasing relationship with the cell-cell repulsion parameter, ci (PRCC: 0.78, p<0.0001) and almost no correlation for the filopodial radius (PRCC: 0.05, p=0.07).
evidence: This is determined from correlation analysis of the simulation results shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5.

claim: There is almost no correlation between the nearest neighbor distance and the filopodial radius.
source: Scatter plots (Figure 2—figure supplement 5) suggest a monotonically decreasing relationship between the nearest neighbor distance and the cell-ECM weight, χ (PRCC: –0.74, p<0.0001), a monotonically increasing relationship with the cell-cell repulsion parameter, ci (PRCC: 0.78, p<0.0001) and almost no correlation for the filopodial radius (PRCC: 0.05, p=0.07).
evidence: This is determined from correlation analysis of the simulation results shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5.

claim: When leader secretory cells secrete FN puncta more rapidly, the stream travels further, by roughly 18%.
source: When leader secretory cells secrete FN puncta more rapidly, we find that the stream travels further, by roughly 18%.
evidence: This is determined from simulated gain-of-function experiments shown in Figure 3A.

claim: If neither cell type secretes new FN puncta, then the average distance the stream travels decreases by about 5%.
source: By contrast, if neither cell type secretes new FN puncta, then the average distance the stream travels decreases by about 5% (collective migration still occurs because cells can respond to pre-existing FN).
evidence: This is determined from simulated loss-of-function experiments shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Collective migration still occurs in the ABM when neither cell type secretes FN because cells can respond to pre-existing FN.
source: By contrast, if neither cell type secretes new FN puncta, then the average distance the stream travels decreases by about 5% (collective migration still occurs because cells can respond to pre-existing FN).
evidence: This is an explanation for why migration still occurs in the no-secretion condition.

claim: If both cell types secrete FN at the baseline rate, then the average distance migrated by cells decreases by 21% from the baseline levels.
source: Finally, if both cell types secrete FN, such that there is no difference between cell phenotypes, then the average distance migrated by cells decreases from the baseline levels regardless of whether secretion occurs at the baseline rate (21% decrease) or is elevated (19% decrease).
evidence: This is determined from simulated experiments shown in Figure 3A.

claim: If both cell types secrete FN at an elevated rate, then the average distance migrated by cells decreases by 19% from the baseline levels.
source: Finally, if both cell types secrete FN, such that there is no difference between cell phenotypes, then the average distance migrated by cells decreases from the baseline levels regardless of whether secretion occurs at the baseline rate (21% decrease) or is elevated (19% decrease).
evidence: This is determined from simulated experiments shown in Figure 3A.

claim: When leading secretory cells are unable to remodel the matrix, the average distance traveled by the NCC stream decreases by 47%.
source: When leading secretory cells (or both cell types) are unable to remodel the matrix, the average distance traveled by the NCC stream decreases by 47% (resp. 51%).
evidence: This is determined from simulated loss-of-function experiments shown in Figure 3B.

claim: When both cell types are unable to remodel the matrix, the average distance traveled by the NCC stream decreases by 51%.
source: When leading secretory cells (or both cell types) are unable to remodel the matrix, the average distance traveled by the NCC stream decreases by 47% (resp. 51%).
evidence: This is determined from simulated loss-of-function experiments shown in Figure 3B.

claim: When follower 'non-secretory' cells are prevented from assembling and reorienting FN fibers, the effect is minimal with only a 2% reduction in distance traveled.
source: When follower 'non-secretory' cells are prevented from assembling and reorienting FN fibers, however, the effect is minimal with only a 2% reduction in distance traveled.
evidence: This is determined from simulated loss-of-function experiments shown in Figure 3B.

claim: FN remodeling by leading NCCs plays a key role in determining long-distance collective migration within the ABM.
source: These results demonstrate that, within the ABM, FN remodeling by leading NCCs plays a key role in determining long-distance collective migration.
evidence: This is concluded from the simulated experiments shown in Figure 3B.

claim: No discernible differences are observed in the ABM when trailing cells cannot remodel the matrix.
source: By contrast, no discernible differences are observed when trailing cells cannot remodel the matrix.
evidence: This is determined from the simulated experiments shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Collective migration may be made more effective when leading and trailing NCCs perform specialized roles, with leading cells remodeling the ECM.
source: Our findings suggest that collective migration may be made more effective when leading and trailing NCCs perform specialized roles, with leading cells remodeling the ECM.
evidence: This is concluded from the simulated experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: Increasing the initial lattice spacing between FN puncta from 20 to 60 µm hinders collective migration in the ABM, decreasing the distance that the stream migrates by 36%.
source: Increasing the initial lattice spacing between FN puncta from 20 to 60 µm hinders collective migration in the ABM, decreasing the distance that the stream migrates by 36%.
evidence: This is determined from simulated experiments shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The lateral spread of NCCs is reduced within sparser matrices.
source: The lateral spread of NCCs is similarly reduced within sparser matrices (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is determined from simulated experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: If NCCs are less likely to sense FN in their local environment, then they are consequently less likely to migrate as far.
source: We conclude that if NCCs are less likely to sense FN in their local environment, then they are consequently less likely to migrate as far.
evidence: This is concluded from the simulated experiments with sparser FN matrices.

claim: The nearest neighbor distance between cells decreases in sparser FN matrices.
source: Additionally, the nearest neighbor distance between cells decreases (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is determined from simulated experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Increased cell density and low motility state in sparser matrices resembles a 'jamming' scenario in which cells are tightly packed, resistant to movement, and behave like a solid.
source: Such an increased cell density and low motility state resembles a 'jamming' scenario in which cells are tightly packed, resistant to movement, and behave like a solid (Sadati et al., 2013).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the simulation results based on the concept of jamming from the literature.

claim: Cells in the ABM are classified as being in a 'jammed' state when they collectively travel less than 100 µm over 12 hr.
source: These similarities lead us to classify cells in the ABM as being in a 'jammed' state when they collectively travel less than 100 µm over 12 hr, as we have found a moderate but statistically significant positive correlation between the nearest neighbor distance and the distance traveled in the horizontal direction (Figure 2—figure supplement 7; Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a definition based on the correlation analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 7.

claim: If contact guidance is upregulated in the ABM in sparse FN, then the NCC migration distance increases by 67%.
source: If contact guidance is upregulated in the ABM (e.g. if the weight χ decreases from 0.5 to 0.33), then the NCC migration distance in sparse FN increases by 67%.
evidence: This is determined from simulated rescue experiments shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Upregulating contact guidance in sparse FN causes the migration distance to exceed that obtained in the denser (20 µm) FN lattice by 7%.
source: The distance exceeds that obtained in the denser (20 µm) FN lattice by 7%.
evidence: This is determined from simulated rescue experiments shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Increasing the cell-cell repulsion strength in sparse FN causes NCCs to travel 44% greater distances.
source: Increasing the cell-cell repulsion strength or the rate at which secretory cells produce FN also cause NCCs to travel greater distances within the sparser FN matrix (by 44% and 28%, respectively), but these changes do not rescue migration to distances comparable to those in denser environments.
evidence: This is determined from simulated rescue experiments shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Increasing the rate at which secretory cells produce FN in sparse FN causes NCCs to travel 28% greater distances.
source: Increasing the cell-cell repulsion strength or the rate at which secretory cells produce FN also cause NCCs to travel greater distances within the sparser FN matrix (by 44% and 28%, respectively), but these changes do not rescue migration to distances comparable to those in denser environments.
evidence: This is determined from simulated rescue experiments shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Increasing cell-cell repulsion or FN secretion rate do not rescue migration to distances comparable to those in denser environments.
source: Increasing the cell-cell repulsion strength or the rate at which secretory cells produce FN also cause NCCs to travel greater distances within the sparser FN matrix (by 44% and 28%, respectively), but these changes do not rescue migration to distances comparable to those in denser environments.
evidence: This is determined from simulated rescue experiments shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Contact guidance, ECM remodeling, and/or cell-cell repulsion are important in rescuing long-distance migration when cells are in a jammed state.
source: These results highlight the importance of contact guidance, ECM remodeling, and/or cell-cell repulsion in rescuing long-distance migration, even when cells are in a jammed state where migration is otherwise hindered.
evidence: This is concluded from the simulated rescue experiments shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Mechanisms that generate collective migration do not guarantee that cells robustly travel along a single target corridor.
source: As noted above, mechanisms that generate collective migration do not guarantee that cells robustly travel along a single target corridor.
evidence: This is concluded from the observation that streams branch in the ABM.

claim: ABM simulations have generated NCC streams that typically spread out to widths almost double that of the neural tube corridor from which they emerge.
source: Thus far, our ABM simulations have generated NCC streams that typically spread out to widths almost double that of the neural tube corridor from which they emerge.
evidence: This is an observation from the simulation results.

claim: In vivo streams typically maintain a constant width from the neural tube and do not branch.
source: By contrast, in vivo streams typically maintain a constant width from the neural tube and do not branch (Szabó et al., 2016; Kulesa et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous experimental studies.

claim: The guiding force reduces lateral migration from the target corridor as its 'strength', z, increases.
source: The guiding force indeed reduces lateral migration from the target corridor as its 'strength', z, increases.
evidence: This is determined from simulated experiments shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The NCC stream narrows by as much as 71% when the guiding force acts on both cell types.
source: The NCC stream narrows by as much as 71% when the guiding force acts on both cell types or by 88% when the force only affects leading cells (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is determined from simulated experiments shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The NCC stream narrows by 88% when the guiding force only affects leading cells.
source: The NCC stream narrows by as much as 71% when the guiding force acts on both cell types or by 88% when the force only affects leading cells (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is determined from simulated experiments shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Cells migrate longer distances along the corridor when the guiding force is present.
source: Cells also migrate longer distances along the corridor (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is determined from simulated experiments shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The distance migrated is linearly correlated with the guiding force strength when the force acts on leader cells only.
source: As we expected, the distance migrated is linearly correlated with the guiding force strength, regardless of whether the guiding force acts on leader cells or on both cell types (leader-only Pearson correlation coefficient: 0.9793, p=0.02; both cell types PCC: 0.9993, p=0.007).
evidence: This is determined from correlation analysis of the simulation results.

claim: The distance migrated is linearly correlated with the guiding force strength when the force acts on both cell types.
source: As we expected, the distance migrated is linearly correlated with the guiding force strength, regardless of whether the guiding force acts on leader cells or on both cell types (leader-only Pearson correlation coefficient: 0.9793, p=0.02; both cell types PCC: 0.9993, p=0.007).
evidence: This is determined from correlation analysis of the simulation results.

claim: The guiding force can drive leader secretory cells to separate from non-secretory follower cells if the former are the only cell type to experience guiding forces.
source: Improvements in the NCC stream trajectory, however, can also drive leader secretory cells to separate from non-secretory follower cells if the former are the only cell type to experience guiding forces.
evidence: This is determined from simulated experiments shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The distance between leader and follower cells increases with the guiding force strength by up to 160% when the guiding force only affects leaders.
source: In such cases, the distance between leader and follower cells (Figure 4C) increases with the guiding force strength by up to 160%, indicating fragmentation of the NCC stream.
evidence: This is determined from simulated experiments shown in Figure 4C.

claim: No breaks occur when the guiding force acts on both cell types.
source: However, no breaks occur when the guiding force acts on both cell types, as the distance between leader and follower cells decreases slightly with the guiding force strength (by about 15% from its baseline value).
evidence: This is determined from simulated experiments shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The distance between leader and follower cells decreases by about 15% from its baseline value when the guiding force acts on both cell types.
source: However, no breaks occur when the guiding force acts on both cell types, as the distance between leader and follower cells decreases slightly with the guiding force strength (by about 15% from its baseline value).
evidence: This is determined from simulated experiments shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Individual simulations show NCC streams can exhibit chain-like migration, with two or more branches forming that are one to two cells in width.
source: Individual simulations (Figure 4D; Figure 4—video 1) also show NCC streams can exhibit chain-like migration, with two or more branches forming that are one to two cells in width.
evidence: This is demonstrated by simulation results shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Chain-like streams still follow paths of remodeled FN fibers created by leader cells, even when leaders and followers become physically separated.
source: Such chains still follow paths of remodeled FN fibers created by leader cells, even when leaders and followers become physically separated.
evidence: This is observed in the simulation results shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Remodeled ECM can provide a long-range cue for follower cells.
source: This observation supports the idea that remodeled ECM can provide a long-range cue for follower cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that follower cells follow leader-created FN paths even when separated.

claim: Stream breaks can be rescued by increasing the degree to which cell trajectories are influenced by contact guidance.
source: Of all the tested combinations of perturbations (Figure 5A), we find that stream breaks can be rescued by increasing the degree to which cell trajectories are influenced by contact guidance.
evidence: This is determined from simulated rescue experiments shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Upregulating contact guidance in either non-secretory cells or in both cell types reduces distances between leader and follower cells, regardless of what other ABM parameters are altered.
source: Upregulating contact guidance in either non-secretory cells or in both cell types (by decreasing the cell-ECM weight, χ, from 0.5 to 0.33) reduces distances between leader and follower cells, regardless of what other ABM parameters are altered.
evidence: This is determined from simulated rescue experiments shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Stream resistance to fragmentation is sensitive to the strength of the contact guidance cues NCCs receive from nearby ECM.
source: Thus, stream resistance to fragmentation is sensitive to the strength of the contact guidance cues NCCs receive from nearby ECM.
evidence: This is concluded from the simulated rescue experiments shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Enhancing contact guidance in both cell types creates a robust single, ribbon-like stream, with approximately constant width and density.
source: Simulations demonstrate that enhancing contact guidance in both cell types (Figure 5B) creates a robust single, ribbon-like stream, with approximately constant width and density.
evidence: This is demonstrated by simulation results shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Stream breaks can be prevented when leader cells exert weaker repulsive forces than followers.
source: The only other perturbation that successfully prevents the formation of stream breaks occurs when leader cells exert weaker repulsive forces than followers.
evidence: This is determined from simulated rescue experiments shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Streams are less robust to perturbations in other mechanisms when leaders exert weaker repulsive forces than followers.
source: However, these streams are less robust to perturbations in other mechanisms.
evidence: This is determined from simulated rescue experiments shown in Figure 5A.

claim: When leaders exert weaker repulsive forces than followers, multiple stream branches and/or single-file cell chains may form.
source: Furthermore, individual realizations suggest that when leaders exert weaker repulsive forces than followers (Figure 5C), multiple stream branches and/or single-file cell chains may form, even though the distance between cells is approximately constant.
evidence: This is demonstrated by simulation results shown in Figure 5C.

claim: When trailing cells exert stronger repulsive forces than leading cells, additional mechanisms may be required to prevent the emergence of multiple branches and/or single-file cell chains.
source: Thus, when trailing cells exert stronger repulsive forces than leading cells, additional mechanisms may be required to prevent the emergence of multiple branches and/or single-file cell chains.
evidence: This is concluded from the simulation results shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Dynamic deposition and remodeling of FN by a highly invasive cell population can promote collective cell migration over long distances.
source: We demonstrate here how dynamic deposition and remodeling of FN by a highly invasive cell population, such as the neural crest, can promote collective cell migration over long distances.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study based on the combined experimental and modeling results.

claim: Leader chick cranial NCCs have enhanced expression of FN distinct from followers.
source: Our simulations were motivated by several new experimental observations that: (i) leader chick cranial NCCs have enhanced expression of FN distinct from followers (Morrison et al., 2017), (ii) FN protein expression is punctate and disorganized in the mesoderm prior to NCC emigration, (iii) FN becomes filamentous after leader NCCs invade, and (iv) proper levels of FN within the cranial migratory pathways are required for NCC migration (Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study and the experimental data in Figure 1.

claim: Proper levels of FN within the cranial migratory pathways are required for NCC migration.
source: Our simulations were motivated by several new experimental observations that: (i) leader chick cranial NCCs have enhanced expression of FN distinct from followers (Morrison et al., 2017), (ii) FN protein expression is punctate and disorganized in the mesoderm prior to NCC emigration, (iii) FN becomes filamentous after leader NCCs invade, and (iv) proper levels of FN within the cranial migratory pathways are required for NCC migration (Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Contact guidance and ECM remodeling are sufficient to support collective behavior in the ABM.
source: In agreement with mathematical models for collective cell migration in mature ECM, we found that contact guidance and ECM remodeling are sufficient to support collective behavior (Painter, 2009), with the establishment of ECM fibers an important step in enabling long-distance migration (Azimzade et al., 2019; Suveges et al., 2021; Metzcar et al., 2022).
evidence: This is concluded from the modeling results and supported by citations to previous modeling studies.

claim: The establishment of ECM fibers is an important step in enabling long-distance migration.
source: In agreement with mathematical models for collective cell migration in mature ECM, we found that contact guidance and ECM remodeling are sufficient to support collective behavior (Painter, 2009), with the establishment of ECM fibers an important step in enabling long-distance migration (Azimzade et al., 2019; Suveges et al., 2021; Metzcar et al., 2022).
evidence: This is concluded from the modeling results and supported by citations to previous modeling studies.

claim: Upregulating contact guidance increases the distances that cells travel in the ABM, at the cost of increasing cell separation.
source: Upregulating contact guidance increases the distances that cells travel, at the cost of increasing cell separation.
evidence: This is concluded from the modeling results shown in Figures 2 and 4.

claim: Cells are capable of directed migration by remodeling an initially isotropic ECM.
source: Additionally, we found that cells are capable of directed migration by remodeling an initially isotropic ECM (Park et al., 2020).
evidence: This is concluded from the modeling results and supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: ECM remodeling created a 'memory' for trailing cells in the ABM, since non-secretory cells were still able to migrate along the paths of leading cells even when stream breaks occurred.
source: ECM remodeling also created a 'memory' for trailing cells in the ABM, since non-secretory cells were still able to migrate along the paths of leading cells even when stream breaks occurred.
evidence: This is concluded from the modeling results shown in Figure 4.

claim: The observation that non-secretory cells migrate along leader-created paths is consistent with in vitro observations of individual cell migration.
source: This is consistent with in vitro observations of individual cell migration (d'Alessandro et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous experimental study.

claim: Knocking out FN expression in the ABM significantly reduces the number of NCCs that successfully migrate along the target corridor.
source: We further showed in our ABM that knocking out FN expression significantly reduces the number of NCCs that successfully migrate along the target corridor, which agrees with in vivo experiments of cardiac mice NCCs (Wang and Astrof, 2016).
evidence: This is determined from the modeling results and supported by a citation to a previous experimental study.

claim: Cells in the ABM traveled in the direction of greatest FN concentration.
source: Furthermore, cells in the ABM traveled in the direction of greatest FN concentration, with fibers preferentially oriented in the direction of the stream migration similar to in vitro experiments (Newgreen, 1989; Rovasio et al., 1983).
evidence: This is determined from the modeling results and supported by citations to previous experimental studies.

claim: Fibers in the ABM are preferentially oriented in the direction of the stream migration similar to in vitro experiments.
source: Furthermore, cells in the ABM traveled in the direction of greatest FN concentration, with fibers preferentially oriented in the direction of the stream migration similar to in vitro experiments (Newgreen, 1989; Rovasio et al., 1983).
evidence: This is determined from the modeling results and supported by citations to previous experimental studies.

claim: The model predicts that increased production of FN by follower cells leads to stream separation.
source: In future work, we plan to experimentally test the model prediction that increased production of FN by follower cells leads to stream separation.
evidence: This is a prediction from the modeling results shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The interactions between cells and the ECM in the ABM resemble a 'long-range attraction, short-range repulsion' phenomenon found in other frameworks for NCC migration based on contact inhibition of locomotion.
source: The interactions between cells and the ECM resemble a 'long-range attraction, short-range repulsion' phenomenon found in other frameworks for NCC migration based on contact inhibition of locomotion, where cells repel each other along the direction of contact and attract each other via local chemoattractant secretion (Carmona-Fontaine et al., 2011; Woods et al., 2014; Szabó et al., 2016; Szabó et al., 2019; Khataee et al., 2021).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the model structure and is supported by citations to previous modeling studies.

claim: Unlike other models, upregulating cell-cell repulsion in the ABM did not always increase the distance migrated by cells.
source: Unlike those models, however, upregulating cell-cell repulsion did not always increase the distance migrated by cells.
evidence: This is determined from the modeling results shown in Figure 2.

claim: The difference in the effect of cell-cell repulsion likely arises from the incorporation of alignment cues from ECM remodeling in the ABM.
source: This difference likely arises from the incorporation of alignment cues from ECM remodeling in our ABM as well as the choice to stochastically sample the cell-cell repulsion force direction, as this causes cell-cell repulsion to act antagonistically to mechanisms promoting persistent migration such as contact guidance.
evidence: This is an inference about why the model behaves differently from previous models.

claim: The stochastic sampling of the cell-cell repulsion force direction causes cell-cell repulsion to act antagonistically to mechanisms promoting persistent migration such as contact guidance.
source: This difference likely arises from the incorporation of alignment cues from ECM remodeling in our ABM as well as the choice to stochastically sample the cell-cell repulsion force direction, as this causes cell-cell repulsion to act antagonistically to mechanisms promoting persistent migration such as contact guidance.
evidence: This is an inference about the mechanism underlying the model behavior.

claim: In silico experiments demonstrated the importance of ECM remodeling by leaders of an NCC stream.
source: Further in silico experiments demonstrated the importance of ECM remodeling by leaders of an NCC stream.
evidence: This is concluded from the modeling results shown in Figure 3.

claim: NCCs migrated most persistently in the ABM when leader and follower cells specialized in different roles, with cells at the front guiding NCC streams via FN remodeling.
source: NCCs migrated most persistently when leader and follower cells specialized in different roles, with cells at the front guiding NCC streams via FN remodeling.
evidence: This is concluded from the modeling results shown in Figure 3.

claim: Future experiments that knock down FN production in leaders only will disrupt collective cell migration in vivo.
source: This suggests that future experiments that either knock down FN production in leaders only or disrupt an NCC's ability to align an FN fibril will disrupt collective cell migration in vivo.
evidence: This is a prediction from the modeling results shown in Figure 3.

claim: Future experiments that disrupt an NCC's ability to align an FN fibril will disrupt collective cell migration in vivo.
source: This suggests that future experiments that either knock down FN production in leaders only or disrupt an NCC's ability to align an FN fibril will disrupt collective cell migration in vivo.
evidence: This is a prediction from the modeling results shown in Figure 3.

claim: Simulated rescue experiments suggest more robust streams may result when follower cells travel faster along leader-created paths by upregulating contact guidance and/or cell-cell repulsion.
source: Simulated rescue experiments for stream breaks also suggest more robust streams may result when follower cells travel faster along leader-created paths by upregulating contact guidance and/or cell-cell repulsion.
evidence: This is concluded from the modeling results shown in Figure 5.

claim: Evidence for specialization between leader and follower cells exists in vivo, as chick cranial NCCs exhibit different morphologic and transcriptomic profiles depending on their location within the stream.
source: Evidence for such specialization exists in vivo, as chick cranial NCCs exhibit different morphologic and transcriptomic profiles depending on their location within the stream (Teddy and Kulesa, 2004; McLennan et al., 2015a; Morrison et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous experimental studies.

claim: Delta-Notch signaling is a potential pathway for dynamically modulating leader/follower cell types in zebrafish trunk NCCs.
source: Our findings do not rule out the possibility, however, that leader and follower cells may switch position and behavior as suggested by identification of Delta-Notch signaling as a potential pathway for dynamically modulating leader/follower cell types in zebrafish trunk NCCs (Richardson et al., 2016; Alhashem et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous experimental studies.

claim: The pre-existing FN distribution appeared to be a critical component in establishing collective cell migration in the ABM.
source: The pre-existing FN distribution, and its possible impact on cell jamming, appeared to be a critical component in establishing collective cell migration.
evidence: This is concluded from the modeling results shown in Figure 3.

claim: Cells fail to migrate long distances within sparser matrices in the ABM.
source: As might be expected from in vitro knockdown studies of the FN matrix (Rovasio et al., 1983), cells fail to migrate long distances within sparser matrices in the ABM.
evidence: This is determined from the modeling results shown in Figure 3C and is consistent with previous experimental studies.

claim: Cells could overcome jammed states by upregulating contact guidance, FN secretion, and/or cell-cell repulsion.
source: Interestingly, we found cells could overcome such jammed states by upregulating contact guidance, FN secretion, and/or cell-cell repulsion, suggesting a role for ECM remodeling to resolve jamming conditions.
evidence: This is concluded from the modeling results shown in Figure 3C.

claim: ECM remodeling may play a role in resolving jamming conditions.
source: Interestingly, we found cells could overcome such jammed states by upregulating contact guidance, FN secretion, and/or cell-cell repulsion, suggesting a role for ECM remodeling to resolve jamming conditions.
evidence: This is inferred from the modeling results shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The ABM relies on the assumption that cells migrate in a 2D domain.
source: It relies on the assumptions that cells migrate in a 2D domain, do not divide, and only transiently contact their neighbors.
evidence: This is a description of the model assumptions.

claim: The ABM relies on the assumption that cells do not divide.
source: It relies on the assumptions that cells migrate in a 2D domain, do not divide, and only transiently contact their neighbors.
evidence: This is a description of the model assumptions.

claim: The ABM relies on the assumption that cells only transiently contact their neighbors.
source: It relies on the assumptions that cells migrate in a 2D domain, do not divide, and only transiently contact their neighbors.
evidence: This is a description of the model assumptions.

claim: The ABM assumptions are likely to be satisfied for chick cranial NCC migration.
source: While such criteria are likely to be satisfied for the motivating example of chick cranial NCC migration and for some in vitro experiments on NCCs (Rovasio et al., 1983), they may not be valid for other populations of NCCs such as those in the gut, where proliferation plays a significant role in collective migration (Simpson et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a statement about the applicability of the model assumptions supported by citations.

claim: The ABM assumptions may not be valid for gut NCCs, where proliferation plays a significant role in collective migration.
source: While such criteria are likely to be satisfied for the motivating example of chick cranial NCC migration and for some in vitro experiments on NCCs (Rovasio et al., 1983), they may not be valid for other populations of NCCs such as those in the gut, where proliferation plays a significant role in collective migration (Simpson et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the model supported by a citation.

claim: The ABM did not address the possible roles of phenotype switching and cell shuffling on NCC streams.
source: We also incorporated a relatively small number of mechanisms into the ABM, such that we did not address the possible roles of phenotype switching and cell shuffling on NCC streams (McLennan et al., 2012; McLennan et al., 2015b; Schumacher, 2019).
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the model.

claim: The implementation of cell-cell repulsion in the ABM differs from those previously used in models incorporating contact inhibition of locomotion.
source: Furthermore, our implementation of cell-cell repulsion differs from those previously used in models incorporating contact inhibition of locomotion (Colombi et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a statement about how the model differs from previous models, supported by a citation.

claim: Cells in the ABM can potentially align with each other at long ranges but repel each other at short range.
source: However, while cells in our ABM can potentially align with each other at long ranges, they repel each other at short range, with increases in cell-cell repulsion parameter values leading to greater intercellular distances.
evidence: This is a description of how cell-cell repulsion is implemented in the model.

claim: Increases in cell-cell repulsion parameter values lead to greater intercellular distances in the ABM.
source: However, while cells in our ABM can potentially align with each other at long ranges, they repel each other at short range, with increases in cell-cell repulsion parameter values leading to greater intercellular distances.
evidence: This is determined from the modeling results shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5.

claim: The authors do not anticipate that other formulations of cell-cell repulsion will lead to results that are significantly different from those described in the study.
source: We therefore do not anticipate that other formulations of cell-cell repulsion will lead to results that are significantly different from those described here.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the model behavior.

claim: Many equations governing cell behavior will not change when going from a 2D to a 3D environment.
source: Indeed, many equations governing cell behavior will not change when going from a 2D to a 3D environment.
evidence: This is a statement about how the model could be extended to 3D.

claim: The orientation of FN fibers will need to be described with 3D spherical coordinates rather than 2D polar coordinates in a 3D model.
source: For instance, the orientation of FN fibers will need to be described with 3D spherical coordinates rather than 2D polar coordinates.
evidence: This is a statement about how the model would need to be modified for 3D.

claim: The distributions from which one samples the directions of the haptotactic and cell-cell repulsion forces will have to change to a 3D von Mises-Fisher distribution from a 2D von Mises distribution in a 3D model.
source: The distributions from which one samples the directions of the haptotactic and cell-cell repulsion forces will also have to change to a 3D von Mises-Fisher distribution from a 2D von Mises distribution (Sra, 2012).
evidence: This is a statement about how the model would need to be modified for 3D, supported by a citation.

claim: The impact of jamming may be reduced in a 3D scenario where cells have more freedom to travel out of the plane.
source: It would be interesting to evaluate the impact of 3D settings on cell migration, as the impact of jamming may be reduced in a scenario where cells have more freedom to travel out of the plane.
evidence: This is a speculation about how the model behavior might change in 3D.

claim: The ABM proved useful in providing experimentally testable predictions for in vivo NCC migration.
source: Despite these limitations, the ABM proved useful in providing experimentally testable predictions for in vivo NCC migration.
evidence: This is a statement about the utility of the model.

claim: In vivo signals such as chemotaxis up VEGF gradients and anisotropic domain growth may play a role in correctly steering cell streams.
source: In vivo signals known to affect chick cranial NCC migration, such as chemotaxis up VEGF gradients and anisotropic domain growth (McLennan et al., 2012; McKinney et al., 2020), may play such a role in correctly steering cell streams.
evidence: This is a speculation about what mechanisms might correspond to the guiding force in the model, supported by citations.

claim: Guiding forces alone cannot account for the robustness of streams, as the ABM found that guiding forces made stream breaks more likely to occur.
source: However, these mechanisms alone cannot account for the robustness of streams, as we found in the ABM that the guiding forces made stream breaks more likely to occur.
evidence: This is concluded from the modeling results shown in Figure 4.

claim: The ABM results showing that guiding forces promote stream breaks are consistent with those obtained from more detailed cell-induced chemotaxis models for collective migration.
source: These results are consistent with those obtained from more detailed cell-induced chemotaxis models for collective migration (Giniūnaitė et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous modeling study.

claim: Simulated rescue experiments constitute one of the first comprehensive surveys of mechanisms enabling robust collective NCC migration.
source: Simulated rescue experiments with our ABM, which constitute one of the first comprehensive surveys of mechanisms enabling robust collective NCC migration, suggested that leader-follower separation can be averted when cells upregulate contact guidance or when leading and trailing cells have different strengths of cell repulsion.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the study.

claim: Leader-follower separation can be averted when cells upregulate contact guidance.
source: Simulated rescue experiments with our ABM, which constitute one of the first comprehensive surveys of mechanisms enabling robust collective NCC migration, suggested that leader-follower separation can be averted when cells upregulate contact guidance or when leading and trailing cells have different strengths of cell repulsion.
evidence: This is concluded from the modeling results shown in Figure 5.

claim: Leader-follower separation can be averted when leading and trailing cells have different strengths of cell repulsion.
source: Simulated rescue experiments with our ABM, which constitute one of the first comprehensive surveys of mechanisms enabling robust collective NCC migration, suggested that leader-follower separation can be averted when cells upregulate contact guidance or when leading and trailing cells have different strengths of cell repulsion.
evidence: This is concluded from the modeling results shown in Figure 5.

claim: Future studies will be needed to test the predictions about preventing stream breaks in vivo.
source: Future studies will be needed to test these predictions in vivo, but such results demonstrate the power of data-driven mathematical modeling to explore biological hypotheses and assist with experimental design.
evidence: This is a statement about future work needed to validate the model predictions.

claim: The results demonstrate the power of data-driven mathematical modeling to explore biological hypotheses and assist with experimental design.
source: Future studies will be needed to test these predictions in vivo, but such results demonstrate the power of data-driven mathematical modeling to explore biological hypotheses and assist with experimental design.
evidence: This is a statement about the value of the modeling approach.

claim: At most 10% of NCCs undergo mitosis during the first 12 hr of migration.
source: Prior research indicates that at most 10% of NCCs undergo mitosis during the first 12 hr of migration (Ridenour et al., 2014), which suggests cell division is a negligible contributor to collective cell migration and hence can be ignored in the mathematical model.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous experimental study.

claim: Cell division is a negligible contributor to collective cell migration during the first 12 hr.
source: Prior research indicates that at most 10% of NCCs undergo mitosis during the first 12 hr of migration (Ridenour et al., 2014), which suggests cell division is a negligible contributor to collective cell migration and hence can be ignored in the mathematical model.
evidence: This is inferred from the cited experimental data.

claim: The walltime for a single ABM realization varied between about 90 s and 2 min.
source: The walltime for a single ABM realization varied between about 90 s and 2 min, depending on the number of cells that enter the domain and the number of FN puncta secreted.
evidence: This is a description of the computational performance of the model.

claim: The number of trailing cells that enter the domain using the baseline parameter values ranged from 1 to 140, depending on the success of migration.
source: We found that the number of trailing cells that enter the domain using these parameter values ranged from 1 to 140, depending on the success of migration (Figure 2—figure supplement 8).
evidence: This is determined from analysis of the simulation results shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 8.
